headline: IRGC CONFIRMS the five tankers were targeted, claims 'fierce missile strikes' destroyed hangars at Al-Azraq base (Jordan) and
dek: (1) US destroyed five named Iranian oil tankers after directing crews to abandon ship, in response to two attempted IRGC attacks on a US warship — all personnel accounted for. (2) IRGC retaliated with missile strikes on Al-Azraq base in Jordan and on US destroyers DDG-119/DDG-53, claiming…
sources: US CENTCOM statement (late Oct 20); IRGC/Sepah News + Iranian state TV statements; Al Jazeera mirror (edgeone.app); Straitstimes (Sepah News quotes); Stocktwits/WSJ (prices); ANZ/Kpler via WSJ
fault_line: Is Iran forcing Trump to lift the blockade before the Nov 3 midterms, or drifting into a full naval war? (carry-over from 05:00 record, confirmed live in comments)

sections.what_happened: (1) US destroyed five named Iranian oil tankers after directing crews to abandon ship, in response to two attempted IRGC attacks on a US warship — all personnel accounted for. (2) IRGC retaliated with missile strikes on Al-Azraq base in Jordan and on US destroyers DDG-119/DDG-53, claiming destroyed hangars and 'significant damage' to the vessels.
sections.what_verified: CENTCOM statement via Al Jazeera: IRGC 'sought to target a US warship twice over the past two days' — vessel 'successfully evaded', 'no American personnel were harmed'; crews ordered to abandon ship before strikes; video published of Riesco sinking. IRGC confirmed via Sepah News/state TV that five tankers were targeted (upgrades the 05:00 'US sank five tankers' from Iran-attributed to mutual acknowledgment). Sepah News/Straitstimes: IRGC claims three tankers hit naval mines in southern strait Oct 20 (2M+ barrel tanker 'deactivated all radar'). ANZ/Kpler via WSJ: at least 18 vessels hit in past two weeks. Brent $109.80, WTI ~$98.7 (WSJ). Diplomacy: Rubio (Oct 20) — peace deal 'extremely difficult', economic pressure continues until ship attacks halt; Araghchi (Al-Ikhbariya/IRIB): strait stays closed until US accepts Tehran's conditions, 'Seven-Day Plan' reopening timetable, indirect talks via Pakistan and Qatar continue.
sections.what_disputed: CENTCOM explicitly rejects the mine narrative: 'Iranian claims that tankers are hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz are false. We have cleared the international waterways ... of mines. Iran uses missiles and drones in its aggression' (Newsquawk via straits.live, from 0500 record). IRGC claims of destroyed hangars at Al-Azraq and damage to DDG-119/DDG-53 have NO US confirmation — CENTCOM says evasion and no personnel harmed, contradicting 'significant damage' framing. CENTCOM blockade statement (via meleleh live): blockade 'impartially against vessels of all nations entering or departing Iranian ports'; IRGC warns any military vessel approaching the strait violates ceasefire.
sections.why_matters: The naming of ships and the sinking video turn Oct 20 from claims into CENTCOM-verified escalation; the mine-vs-missile dispute is the honest center — both sides' claims labeled on screen. The IRGC destroyer-damage claims may appear ONLY as Iran-attributed claims with CENTCOM's 'no personnel harmed / evaded' counterpoint. Map-spine Short with the five named tanker locations + Al-Azraq (Jordan) base strikes.
sections.context: Background: Hormuz — UPDATE on totw-20261021-0500-01/1100-06: CENTCOM NAMES the five Iranian tankers it destroyed (M/T Kaviz, M/T Charminar, M/T Horizon 1, M/T Riesco in the Gulf of Oman; M/T Derya near Kharg island) and releases video of the M/T Riesco sinking; IRGC CONFIRMS the five tankers were targeted, claims 'fierce missile strikes' destroyed hangars at Al-Azraq base (Jordan) and that ballistic missiles caused 'significant damage' to US destroyers DDG-119 and DDG-53
